title: unwrapOr cannot reach a panic, because a panicking function publishes no Result to recover from
notes: MANDATORY GUARD, and the direct enforcement of specification/failures.mdx: 'Ordinary Result recovery MUST NOT swallow panic implicitly.' §Panic Does Not Widen a Return Type gives the reasoning in the same words: 'Requiring a panicking function to return Result<A, Panic> places the panic inside E, where unwrapOr, recover, and match consume it as an ordinary failure — which is precisely what this page forbids.' The declared code is the stock TypeScript member-resolution error rather than a SMITHERS rule, and that is the point: the recovery surface does not exist, so there is nothing for a language rule to refuse. This case declares a TS code, so per conformance/README.md it must record the evidence: the position and the code were measured identically on BOTH backends (js TS2339@11:26, go TS2339@11:26), and the message fragment is declared because code and position alone would also be satisfied by a TS2339 about some other member — the whole promise is that `unwrapOr` specifically is unreachable. It is the first case to go red if a later change widens this rule into 'a panic is not tracked' or restores the forced Result. Its accepted twin is 09-foreign-calls/only-an-explicit-boundary-observes-a-panic-from-a-plain-function, which shows what an author writes instead.
